payload.name: Verify-Memory-Coverage-Before-Skip
payload.description: When deciding whether to SKIP a construction candidate because it is 'already fully represented in existing memory', first verify that the retrieved existing-memory pool actually contains a memory covering the candidate's claims. Apply before finalizing any SKIP decision.
content: During the CRUD decision stage, never SKIP a candidate with the reason 'already fully represented in existing memory' unless a memory in the retrieved pool explicitly covers the candidate's claims (same subject, event or state, and key details).
If the retrieved pool contains no such covering memory, the candidate is not yet stored; choose ADD (or MERGE only when the candidate extends an existing memory) instead of SKIP.
A memory that is thematically similar or mentions the same subject but omits the specific claim does not count as coverage.

solves: The diagnosed failure was a SKIP where no existing memory covered the candidate, causing a supported fact to never be persisted. The reusable mechanism is unverified SKIPs based on an assumption of coverage. This rule applies to any future construction session where a candidate is skipped as 'already represented' but the retrieved memory pool lacks an equivalent memory; it does not apply when the pool genuinely contains a covering memory, where SKIP remains correct.
